notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical text: title Dynamic adjustments in working memory in the face of affective interference; authors J. E. Witkin, A. P. Zanesco, E. Denkova, A. P. Jha; DOI 10.3758/s13421-019-00958-w; Memory & Cognition (2020) 48:16–31, published online 5 August 2019. Full published primary research report, including both experiments, analyses, tables, discussion and references; not an abstract or secondary article. No PDF was supplied. Assigned study_r 2 suggests Experiment 2. Description does not distinguish accuracy from RT, current- versus previous-trial demand, main effects versus follow-up comparisons. No row-order or numerical matching used. Experiment 2 previous-load main-effect candidates: accuracy F(1, 6530) = 15.37, p < .001 (printed p.25, PDF page 10); RT F(1, 6530) = 24.64, p = .027 AS PRINTED (printed p.26, PDF page 11). RT follow-up beta = –36.11 has p < .001 and dz = 0.21; this is a different test and its p must not replace the main-effect p. Other candidate mnemonic-load main effects: current-load accuracy F(1,6530) = 111.33, p < .001; current-load RT F(1,6530) = 434.25, p < .001. Table 4 prints log-odds/RT parameter estimates; no conversion performed. Common Experiment 2 model candidate Nobs = 6,612 trial observations nested within 76 retained participants; 100 recruited, 24 excluded for diagnoses/psychotropic medications, no RT outlier trials, remaining participants responded to more than one third of trials. Counts explicit, not inferred from df or summed. As the row-specific test is unresolved, model N is only a candidate for parent field-scope review. Authors explicitly describe replication of the mnemonic-demand result over two experiments (p.29); reported_success is that broad narrative verdict, not a verdict on every interaction/contrast. Locator p.6 (printed p.21) contains Experiment 1 current-trial accuracy/RT analyses, not Experiment 2. It prints mnemonic-load accuracy F(1, 6939) = 106.73, p < .001 and RT F(1, 6939) = 369.74, p < .001; neither can be silently substituted for an Experiment 2 target.
